note: Generated by design/tools/boss_polyrhythm.py. World units. A rotor is a regular polygon of `sides` sides, radius rotorRadius, with an inner copy at 0.5 turning the other way; the numbers are the fight.

numbers.rule: each rotor fires a ring on each of its pulses: every corner throws a solid arc of light, a wall 10 wu thick that grows outward, and its flat faces throw nothing, so every ring has one gap in front of every face. These are walls, not bullets: there is no slipping between them, only through the gaps (or a Dash). A Nova erases every wall it touches. The faces are glass with a gold core behind: the only place a rotor can be hurt. Stand in a gap and the face in front of you is open to your shots
numbers.turn: a rotor turns turnDeg between pulses, so its gaps step round: Three's by 40 degrees three times a bar, Four's by 22.5 degrees four times a bar. Both come back to where they started every bar, and on beat 1 a face of each looks straight at the other: for that pulse both rings have their gap on the link
numbers.theOne: beat 1 of every bar: both fire together and both of those rings have a gap along the link, so they pass either side of anyone standing on it, and each rotor's face is open down its own gap. Rings fired on the other pulses still cross the link: the One is a moment, not a shelter

link.note: a white line from Three to Four ruled into twelve: the bar in twelfths. A playhead runs along it once a bar. Three's ticks (0, 4, 8) are its colour, Four's (0, 3, 6, 9) are its colour, tick 0 is gold. The next tick to fire glows a beat ahead: the link is the score of the fight

numbers.pivot: the midpoint of the link; it follows the players' centre at 50 wu/s, and the link turns round it once every 8 bars

camera.note: eased over the entrance bar; both rotors in the frame

phases.name: Three against four
phases.when: both alive, above 60% of their joint health
phases.note: the pattern as ruled. Learn the One, then learn to ride one rotor's gap round while stepping through the other's rings

phases.name: Hemiola
phases.turn: each rotor reverses its turn every bar

linkBeam.note: the link shows danger dashes for a bar and then burns: the aisle is still safe on the One, but nobody can live in it

phases.note: the gaps now swing back and forth instead of circling

phases.name: Solo
phases.survivor: fires both patterns from its own body: its own ring on its own pulses and the dead rotor's count on a second ring that turns the other way. The gaps of the two rings line up once a bar, on the One, in front of one face
phases.move: it walks toward the nearest player at 70 wu/s
phases.note: kill them close together and this phase is short; kill one early and the other carries both parts for a long time

numbers.contact: a rotor hurts; the link does not, except while it burns

music.three: the tom, tuned to the Track's root, on Three's pulses (twelfths 0, 4, 8)
music.four: the rim, tuned to the flat second, on Four's pulses (twelfths 0, 3, 6, 9)
music.theOne: both and the gong on beat 1
music.pitch: each drum rises a semitone for every quarter of its rotor's health lost
music.solo: the survivor plays both drums at its own pitch
music.note: three against four is audible from the first bar; a player can dodge with their eyes shut once they have the pattern

look.three: a triangle in the palette's cyan with a smaller triangle turning the other way inside it; corners are bright nodes that glint the twelfth before they fire
look.four: a square in the palette's amber, built the same way
look.faces: each flat face is a pane of glass with a gold bar behind it: gold is the weak point
look.rings: walls are arcs in the danger colour on the priority layer, 3 px with the threat rim, like every threat; they thin to 2 px in their last half second; the gaps are plainly empty
look.aisle: on the One a white flare runs the length of the link and a faint white corridor shows through both sets of rings

numbers.entrance: on the Drop's downbeat Three drops in on beat 1 and Four on beat 3, each landing with its drum; the link draws itself between them over the next bar, tick by tick; the name card POLYRHYTHM holds for two bars; firing starts on bar 3
numbers.death: the first rotor to die spins down over a bar and bursts on the One. When the second dies the link's playhead runs one last bar with every tick firing as a ring of sparks instead of bullets, then the boss break on the One: three rings, 300 sparks, the 30 px distortion ring, 50 ms hit-stop, 240 Shards
numbers.coop: health x (1 + 0.5 x (players - 1)); the pivot follows the players' centre; in Solo the survivor walks toward the nearest player
